dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the  Maritime Zones of India (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981 
The Maritime Zones of India (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981 was enacted by the Parliament of India to regulate fishing activities by foreign vessels in India's maritime zones. The Act aims to protect India's marine resources, prevent unauthorized fishing, conserve fish stocks, and safeguard the interests of Indian fishermen. It came into force on 2 November 1981.
Objectives
The main objectives of the Act are to:
•	Regulate fishing by foreign fishing vessels in India's maritime zones. 
•	Conserve and sustainably manage marine fishery resources. 
•	Prevent illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing by foreign vessels. 
•	Protect the livelihood and interests of Indian fishermen. 
•	Ensure that foreign fishing operations are carried out only with the permission of the Central Government. 
Scope of the Act
The Act applies to foreign fishing vessels operating in the maritime zones of India, including:
•	The territorial waters. 
•	The contiguous zone. 
•	The exclusive economic zone (EEZ). 
•	Other maritime zones declared under Indian law. 
It does not generally regulate fishing by Indian fishing vessels, which are governed by other laws.
Licensing of Foreign Fishing Vessels
The Act requires that:
•	No foreign fishing vessel may fish in India's maritime zones without a valid licence issued by the Central Government. 
•	Licences are granted subject to prescribed conditions, including: 
o	Area of operation. 
o	Type of fishing. 
o	Duration of the licence. 
o	Reporting and operational requirements. 
•	The Government may suspend, cancel, or refuse to renew a licence if licence conditions or legal requirements are violated. 
Powers of Enforcement
The Act authorizes designated officers to:
•	Board and inspect foreign fishing vessels. 
•	Examine licences and related documents. 
•	Search vessels suspected of violations. 
•	Seize fishing gear, catch, equipment, or the vessel where necessary. 
•	Arrest persons involved in offences under the Act. 
•	Detain vessels pending legal proceedings. 
Offences and Penalties
The Act prescribes penalties for offences such as:
•	Fishing without a valid licence. 
•	Violating licence conditions. 
•	Obstructing authorized officers in the performance of their duties. 
•	Providing false information or documents. 
•	Engaging in unauthorized fishing activities. 
Penalties may include:
•	Imprisonment. 
•	Monetary fines. 
•	Confiscation of the vessel, fishing gear, catch, or equipment. 
•	Cancellation or suspension of licences.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021
Key Provisions and Impacts
1.	Repealed Legislation: - 1. The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020
•	Impact: Abolishes contractual farming reforms, reverting to pre-2020 arrangements for farmer-producer agreements.
•	The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020
•	Impact: Ends the facilitation of interstate and e-commerce trade of agricultural produce outside traditional mandis, potentially reinstating previous regulatory frameworks.
•	The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020
•	Impact: Removes the 2020 amendments, which had liberalized the control over essential commodities, possibly tightening regulations on stockholding limits and price controls.
2.	Amendment: - Affected Act: The Essential Commodities Act, 1955
•	Change: Omission of Sub-section (1A) of Section 3
•	Implication: Reverts the regulatory framework for declaring commodities as essential, impacting how the government manages supply and prices of critical goods.
Broader Implications and Considerations
•	Policy Reversal: Undoes the 2020 reforms aimed at market liberalization and contractual farming, reflecting a shift in policy approach to agricultural regulation.
•	Regulatory Reversion: For essential commodities and trade practices, the legal framework may revert to a more controlled pre-2020 state, with potential impacts on market dynamics and consumer prices.
•	Omissions in Provided Context:
•	Detailed Rationale for Repeal: Not specified in the context, implying the need for external information to understand the political, social, or economic motivations.
•	Full Pre-Repeal Legal Framework: Partially outlined, suggesting a need for additional legal context to fully grasp the implications of the repeal on agricultural trade, pricing, and contractual agreements.

Legislative History: 
The Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021

Source: Official Records of Parliament, India Code, and Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers Welfare)

Act Title - The Farm Laws Repeal Act, 2021
Act Number - Act No. 40 of 2021
Act ID (India Code) - 202140
Presidential Assent Date - November 30, 2021
Enforcement Date - November 30, 2021
Nodal Ministry -Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 

Precedent & Historical Rationale
Farmer Agitations and Nationwide Protests:
•	Following the enactment of the three contentious farm ordinances in mid-2020 and their subsequent passage as acts in September 2020, widespread protests and prolonged agitations erupted, predominantly led by farmer unions primarily stationed around the borders of New Delhi.
•	The legislative measures aimed at deregulating agricultural trade, enabling contract farming, and amending stock limit rules faced severe opposition from agricultural communities concerned about minimum support prices (MSP), market security, and corporate dominance in the agricultural sector.
Legislative Intent and Repeal Mandate:
•	In response to sustained demonstrations and after months of dialogue, the government announced its decision to repeal the contested legislations in the interest of the nation's farmers and national unity.
•	The Act was formulated to formally rescind the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020, the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020, and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020, while restoring the original framework of the parent Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

Parliamentary Trajectory & Enactment
•	Formulation: Drafted rapidly by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to execute the executive policy decision to roll back the three farm statutes.
•	Parliamentary Passage: Introduced, debated, and passed by both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) during the opening days of the winter session of Parliament in November 2021 without prolonged legislative committee referral.
•	Presidential Assent: Received Presidential Assent on November 30, 2021.
•	Enforcement: Brought into force immediately upon receiving assent on November 30, 2021, marking the formal statutory closure of the 2020 agricultural reform laws.

indexableObject.name: Victim compensation scheme.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
(1) Every State Government in co-ordination with the Central Government shall prepare a scheme for providing funds for the purpose of compensation to the victim or his dependents who have suffered loss or injury as a result of the crime and who require rehabilitation.
(2) Whenever a recommendation is made by the Court for compensation, the District Legal Service Authority or the State Legal Service Authority, as the case may be, shall decide the quantum of compensation to be awarded under the scheme referred to in sub-section (1).
(3) If the trial Court, at the conclusion of the trial, is satisfied, that the compensation awarded under section 395 is not adequate for such rehabilitation, or where the cases end in acquittal or discharge and the victim has to be rehabilitated, it may make recommendation for compensation.
(4) Where the offender is not traced or identified, but the victim is identified, and where no trial takes place, the victim or his dependents may make an application to the State or the District Legal Services Authority for award of compensation.
(5) On receipt of such recommendations or on the application under sub-section (4), the State or the District Legal Services Authority shall, after due enquiry award adequate compensation by completing the enquiry within two months.
(6) The State or the District Legal Services Authority, as the case may be, to alleviate the suffering of the victim, may order for immediate first-aid facility or medical benefits to be made available free of cost on the certificate of the police officer not below the rank of the officer in charge of the police station or a Magistrate of the area concerned, or any other interim relief as the appropriate authority deems fit.
(7) The compensation payable by the State Government under this section shall be in addition to the payment of fine to the victim under section 65, section 70 and sub-section (1) of section 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (45 of 2023).

Provided that if it appears to the Commissioner that the site of the proposed building or work is likely to be affected by any scheme of acquisition of land for any public purpose or by any proposed regular line of a public street or extension, improvement, widening or alteration of any street, the Commissioner may withhold sanction of the building or work for such period not exceeding three months as he deems fit and the period of sixty days or as the case may be, the period of thirty days specified in this sub-section shall be deemed to commence from the date of the expiry of the period for which the sanction has been withheld.

(3) If the person or anyone lawfully claiming under him does not commence the erection of the building or the execution of the work within one year of the date on which the building or work is sanctioned or is deemed to have been sanctioned, he shall have to give notice under section 333 or, as the case may, be under section 334 for fresh sanction of the building or the work and the provisions of this section shall apply in relation to such notice as they apply in relation to the original notice.
(4) Before commencing the erection of a building or execution of a work within the period specified in sub-section (3), the person concerned shall give notice to the Commissioner of the proposed date of the commencement of the erection of the building or the execution of the work:
